recon.variance_source: Where visible, error bars are the standard error of the mean.
recon.control_definition: Ambient CO2 with no ring structures in place; actual CO2 approximately 370-425 ppm (ambient atmospheric concentration at the site in 1999-2000)
recon.treatment_definition: FACE plots with CO2 target of 200 ppmv above ambient; actual 1-min mean values averaged across rings were 625±3 ppmv in 1999 and 570±2 ppmv in 2000
recon.potential_tc_confusion: Minimal risk of T/C swap as grey=ambient/control and black=elevated/treatment is clearly stated in figure legends. However, note that the elevated CO2 level differs between years (625 vs 570 ppm) which may need to be recorded separately.
recon.sample_size_source: There were four blocks consisting of a FACE and ambient plot located in separate paddies having similar soils and agronomic histories.
recon.factorial_structure: ["CO2 (ambient vs elevated)", "Year (1999 vs 2000)", "N level (40, 90, 150 kg/ha - but only 90 kg/ha used for elemental analysis)"]
recon.extraction_guidance: PRIMARY OUTCOME DATA are in Figure 1 (elemental concentrations in grain). Extract values from bar graphs for each element separately for 1999 and 2000. Use grey bars as control (ambient) and black bars as treatment (elevated CO2). n=4 for each bar. Error bars represent SE. Note that micro-nutrients (Zn, Cu, Fe, Mn, B, Co, Mo, Se) are in inserted sub-graphs with different y-axis scales. Only N is statistically significant (P<0.05); record significance as ns for all other elements. For Fig. 2 (elemental removal amounts), note these represent concentration × yield and are averaged across years - these are secondary outcomes for this meta-analysis. Elevated CO2 levels differ between years (625 ppm in 1999, 570 ppm in 2000) - consider reporting year-specific data from Fig. 1 with corresponding CO2 levels. Digital graph extraction software (e.g., WebPlotDigitizer) will be needed as no numerical tables are provided. Be cautious of the scale change between main graphs and inserted micro-nutrient sub-graphs in both figures.
